judgements.justification: In A, Reviewer_g3MG ('a bit beyond my expertise') and Reviewer_cSRr ('unable to assess the soundness') raised to 7 on clarifications and a promised rewrite, with no new results and no check of proofs, and those 7s carried the spotlight.
The committees did not read the paper as the same kind of contribution: A judged a novel coupling-causality link, B a causal-identification method (R16), so this is not one type held to two bars.
A's g3MG Gumbel-softmax error was a criticism, not praise, and no reviewer's praise or score rested on a wrong factual claim about novelty or results.
No B reviewer replied to the rebuttal or said a concern was resolved; ybLo and gci3 never posted again and XBKm's edit only added that the writing needs work.
A credited the promised rewrite, but B's chair rejected on the premise and readability and never refused to credit promised revisions.
No reviewer stated a changed position that differed from an unedited score; eGhr's positive text with a 5 is an original mismatch, not a stated change, and the AC ignored it.
Neither committee's AC called in an additional off-record reviewer.
Reviewers in both committees found the paper hard to read; no domain expert in either committee called it clear.
All three A raises came with stated reasons in posts (g3MG, cSRr, 4cdP), and no B reviewer raised a score.
A's AC left eGhr's 5 unmentioned but did not discount it for non-engagement, and with three 7s it did not decide the outcome.
No A reviewer rated above 7 or checked the core; A's confidences were 3, 3, 2, 2, so A had no invested champion.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading at high confidence; XBKm, who did not get the details, rated at confidence 2.

B's ybLo and AC read the paper from Pearl's identification tradition, made the unfalsifiable choice of mechanism and the monotonicity alternative central, while A accepted the level-2/level-3 framing and judged within it.
A's meta-review argued only that the replies 'cleared up these concerns' and a majority found it 'worth publishing', yet the paper became a spotlight with no reason given for the tier.

Neither committee checked baselines against published results; both missed that the inverse CDF matches or beats the gadgets in Table 1, and B's literature points (Lu et al., monotonicity) concerned the premise, not baselines.
B's meta-review accurately describes three below-threshold reviewers, and A's 'majority agreed' matches the record; no misstatement toward a lower decision.
Neither committee raised a narrow-audience or wrong-venue objection.
B rejected, and A had no misreading detractor whose score kept its chair arguing only acceptance; A gave a spotlight.
A received clarifications, parameter settings and a running example, not new experiments; neither committee saw new results.
Neither committee had a high-confidence expert review rating above the others; A's highest confidence was 3 and B's top ratings were below threshold.
No reviewer added a new objection and changed a score after the response period; XBKm's 2021-08-22 edit added only a writing remark and no score change.
The rating gap follows a different judgement of the premise (B's unfalsifiability objection and AC's ATE point), not more lenient scoring of equally favourable assessments.
Neither committee judged a headline claim or title overstated; B's objection was to the premise of choosing a mechanism, not to an overclaim.
A's reviewers rated 7, not marginal-accept 6, and A's chair gave a spotlight, not a poster; B's ratings were below threshold.
